summary_md:
# 582. Expertens dippköp bland fastighetsaktier

**Feed**: sparpodden  
**Published**: 2026-09-14  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

Special Sparpodden episode on Swedish listed real estate with fund manager Gustaf Sällberg, followed by an interview with Logistea's CEO. The guest says property stocks are the cheapest they have been in about 20 years. He puts the weak share prices down mainly to money leaving small-cap and sector funds and to foreign selling as long-term rates rose. He prefers high-yield industrial and logistics property with clean cash flows, is cautious on residential property and developers for now, and names Balder and Sagax as attractive while calling SBB and Corem high-risk.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 BALD-B — Balder | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Guest: trades very cheaply on cash flow and implied net asset value; diversified mix; Finnish residential attractive on a 3-year view.

#### Reasoning

The guest (fund manager) picks Balder as attractive on valuation. It combines residential with hotels, offices and logistics, plus a small project portfolio, and has a track record of strong deals. Its Finnish residential exposure is cheap and should improve over about three years. Erik Selin remains involved as a deal-maker.

#### Sell Triggers

- if the Finnish housing market fails to recover
- if long-term rates rise sharply
- if deal-making discipline weakens after the CEO change

> *"Balder tycker jag handlas väldigt billigt både på kassaflöde och på liksom implicit substans."*

---

### 🟢 SAGA-B — Sagax | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Guest: at about 12-13x earnings with 5-10% growth it is cheap despite a 26% premium; at net asset value it would be an unreasonable 9x.

#### Reasoning

The guest prefers valuing on cash flow over net asset value. Sagax has grown earnings per share every year. Its premium has fallen from about 200% and the earnings multiple is now modest for its quality. Logistics and industrial property offers clean cash flow and a positive yield spread.

#### Sell Triggers

- if growth falls below 5%
- if the premium expands back to stretched levels
- if the yield spread over financing costs narrows

> *"Nu handlas det kanske 12-13 gånger vinsten och kan växa någonstans mellan 5 och 10. Då blir det ju billigt helt plötsligt, trots att man handlas med premien."*

---

### 🟢 CORE-B — Corem | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 40%

77% discount to net asset value but about 75% leverage. Guest suggests at most a small position; biggest upside if it turns around, and Kista has long-term potential.

#### Reasoning

High leverage (about 4x sensitivity) means a small asset-value error wipes out much of the discount. The company has done a lot of balance-sheet work, and Kista and Globen assets give cash flow and long-term potential. The share could double quickly if it turns around, but the guest sees high risk.

#### Sell Triggers

- if asset writedowns continue
- if refinancing fails
- if Kista vacancies rise faster than expected after Ericsson leaves

> *"Så man kanske inte ska vara all in i Corem. Men man kanske kan ha någon enstaka procent"*

---

### ⛔ SBB-D — SBB D | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Main owners hold A/B shares, so they have little incentive to pay D-share dividends. Guest thinks liquidation is likely, and accrued dividends may not count.

#### Reasoning

Game theory: controlling owners hold mostly A/B shares. The guest's own reading is that accrued unpaid D dividends are ignored in a liquidation. Debt is being shifted into subsidiaries. He also advises writing off the old B-share price levels.

#### Sell Triggers

- if SBB resumes dividends including accrued D dividends

> *"Så vad finns det för incitament för dem att betala D-aktieägarna den typen som de inte äger så mycket av istället för att betala sig själva?"*

---

### ⛔ HUFV-A — Hufvudstaden | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Guest: 'stay rich' stock with low cash yield; its discount unlikely to be realised since assets won't be sold.

#### Reasoning

Finest properties but the lowest running yield, roughly 4-5% bond-like returns. The guest wants 10-20% equity returns and there is no catalyst to realise the discount.

#### Sell Triggers

- if asset sales crystallise the discount

> *"Så jag tycker det är lite stay rich att köpa Hufvudstaden. Men ska man get rich, då tycker jag att man ska ta de andra bitarna"*

---

### ⛔ JM — JM | **AVOID** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Housing developers are cyclical ('SSAB of real estate'). Guest does not see a strong lift in the coming year.

#### Reasoning

High fixed costs and a cyclical business. The guest says developers are not a buy-and-hold and should only be owned near a peak; he expects rising long-term rates to keep conditions tough.

#### Sell Triggers

- if housing demand clearly recovers
- if rates fall significantly

> *"Så jag tror inte det är något man bara ska köpa och äga i tio år, ett JM eller ett Besqab till exempel, eller Bonava."*

---

### 🟠 SVEAF — Svea Fastigheter | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Guest calls it a good case after the Klarabo merger but lacks a trigger; prefers logistics names for now.

#### Reasoning

Consolidation brings financing and operating synergies. But building rights tie up net asset value without cash flow, higher rates hurt residential, and there is a risk of over-aggressive buying.

#### Sell Triggers

- if acquisitions become overly aggressive
- if rates keep rising

> *"Jag tycker nog absolut att det är ett bra case."*

---
